memory.content: Every podcast clip must tell a complete story and pass these checks before it counts as done: a clean start (begins at the start of a thought, not mid-sentence), a complete payoff (questions include the full answer, setups include the punchline), a clean end (finishes on a full sentence that lands), a picture check (no faces or charts cropped off), and a caption-only read that makes sense without hearing the episode. Anything that fails is re-cut.
Podcast clips use word-by-word highlighted captions, where each word turns yellow as it's spoken and upcoming words stay white, timed to the speech.

When a shot doesn't crop well to square (for example an over-the-shoulder angle showing the back of one person's head while the other talks), keep the original widescreen frame inside the square with black bars instead of cropping.

Catch quality problems before the owner sees any work. For podcast clips that means judging them as a viewer would, including reviewing frames at every shot change, not just checking that files play, are square and have captions.

Per episode, produce 8 to 12 square captioned clips of about 20 to 90 seconds, each with 3 to 5 X post draft versions. Drafts only; the owner posts. Put the source link in the first reply, not the post. Never invent personal experiences or claims for the owner, and flag that auto-transcripts can mishear names and products.

skills.name: Podcast Clipper
skills.description: When the owner shares a podcast or YouTube episode URL (or a watched channel drops a new episode) and wants 8-12 square captioned clips with X post versions for each.
skills.content:
---
name: Podcast Clipper
description: >-
  When the owner shares a podcast or YouTube episode URL (or a watched channel
  drops a new episode) and wants 8-12 square captioned clips with X post
  versions for each.
---
# Podcast Clipper

Turns one episode into 8-12 square (1080x1080) captioned clips of 20-90s, each with 3-5 X post versions in the owner's voice. Captions are karaoke-style (word-by-word highlight). Every clip gets a sidecar `.srt`. A per-episode `moments.md` and a channel-level log prevent clipping the same moment or episode twice.

## 0. Setup (once per box)
```bash
pip install --user -U yt-dlp faster-whisper "opencv-python-headless<5" numpy onnxruntime
mkdir -p /workspace/podcast-clips/models && curl -fsSL -o /workspace/podcast-clips/models/yolov8n.onnx https://huggingface.co/Kalray/yolov8/resolve/main/yolov8n.onnx
curl -fsSL https://deno.land/install.sh | sh -s -- -y
sudo apt-get install -y ffmpeg fonts-dejavu-core
mkdir -p /workspace/podcast-clips /workspace/podcast-clips/channels
```
Write the five scripts into /workspace/podcast-clips/ if missing (`chmod +x fetch_transcribe.sh`). Notes: faster-whisper 1.2.1 breaks with PyAV 19 when given a file path, so transcribe.py reads the wav with `wave` and passes a numpy array. The box is CPU-only; small.en int8 does a ~100 min episode in roughly 20-40 min, so run it in the background. When rendering in a shell loop, pass `</dev/null` to render_clip.py, or ffmpeg will swallow the loop's input.

## 1. Download + transcribe
`/workspace/podcast-clips/fetch_transcribe.sh <url> <slug>` -> `<slug>/video.mp4`, `video.info.json`, `audio.wav` (16k mono), `transcript.txt`, `words.json`. Use the info.json chapters to orient.

## 1b. Channel log (watched channels)
Before clipping a watched-channel episode, check the channel log so you never re-clip:
```bash
python3 /workspace/podcast-clips/moments.py channel-has <channel_id> <slug> && echo ALREADY_CLIPPED && exit 0
```
After a successful delivery: `python3 moments.py channel-mark <channel_id> <slug> <url>`. Log file: `/workspace/podcast-clips/channels/<channel_id>.json`.

## 2. Pick moments (re-read moments.md first)
If `<slug>/moments.md` exists, read it and skip any candidate whose time range overlaps a row with status `picked` or `cut`. Read transcript.txt. Pick 8-12 moments of 20-90s that match the owner's niche/angles (from memory). Prefer a single clear claim, a surprising number, a sharp question and answer, or a quotable line. Each must stand alone without context. Write `picks.txt`, one per line: `NN HH:MM:SS HH:MM:SS`.

Score every candidate in `moments.md` as `strong`, `maybe`, or `skip`, with status `picked`, `passed`, or leave for later. Create or refresh the log:
```bash
python3 /workspace/podcast-clips/moments.py init <slug-dir> --from-picks
python3 /workspace/podcast-clips/moments.py add <slug-dir> NN HH:MM:SS HH:MM:SS strong "one-line note"
python3 /workspace/podcast-clips/moments.py mark <slug-dir> NN passed
```

## 3. Snap to sentences
`python3 snap.py <slug>/words.json picks.txt` prints exact start/end seconds snapped to segment boundaries plus the text. Adjust picks if a clip starts or ends mid-thought. Update `moments.md` start/end to the snapped times.

## 4. Render
`python3 render_clip.py <slug> NN <start> <end>` for each -> `<slug>/clips/clip-NN.mp4`: face-centred crop per camera shot, burned-in ASS karaoke captions (yellow highlight on the spoken word, white waiting words), H.264 high/yuv420p + AAC, +faststart. Also writes `<slug>/clips/clip-NN.srt` and sets that row's status in `moments.md` to `cut`.

## 5. Verify every clip
```bash
ffprobe -v error -show_entries stream=codec_name,width,height -show_entries format=duration -of compact clip-NN.mp4
ffmpeg -v error -i clip-NN.mp4 -f null -
test -s clip-NN.srt && head -6 clip-NN.srt
```
Grab a frame and look at it: face in frame, captions readable with the active word highlighted (yellow), note any on-screen chart or text cut off by the crop.

## 5b. Story QA (required before delivery)
For every clip, print from words.json the sentence before the start, the clip's sentences, and the next two sentences after the end. Fail and re-cut any clip that misses one of these checks:
1. **Clean start**: opens at the start of a thought, not mid-sentence.
2. **Complete payoff**: a question includes the full answer; a setup includes its punchline. Never end on a question unless the answer is in the clip.
3. **Clean end**: ends on a full sentence that lands. No trailing first words of the next topic, and no new question.
4. **Caption-only read**: reading only the captions makes sense without hearing the episode.
5. **Picture**: extract 4 to 6 frames and look at them. Faces centred; charts not cut off. Over-the-shoulder / no-face shots are letterboxed full-frame. Confirm karaoke highlight is visible.
6. **Overlap**: if two clips cover the same answer, keep the better one. Never cut a range already marked `cut`.
Keep the replaced file as clip-NN-old.mp4, update clips.txt and moments.md, and re-run ffprobe on every changed clip.

## 6. Write posts
For each clip write 3-5 versions following the owner's saved style notes. Rules:
- Hook names who is speaking and why it matters.
- Quote only what the transcript says; flag that auto-transcripts can mishear names and products.
- Never invent personal experiences or claims for the owner.
- Source link goes in the first reply, not the post.
- Drafts only. The owner posts.

## 7. Deliver
Send one message per clip: clip number, start-end timestamps, one-line summary/key quote, any crop or transcript caveats, the post versions, and the MP4 attached. Lead with a short note that all clips are done plus the source link. Mark the channel log if this was a watched-channel episode.

---
## Scripts
On first setup, write these five files into `/workspace/podcast-clips/` if missing (`chmod +x fetch_transcribe.sh`):

1. `fetch_transcribe.sh` - download with yt-dlp, extract 16k mono wav, run transcribe.py
2. `transcribe.py` - faster-whisper small.en int8 on wav via numpy (not PyAV path), write transcript.txt + words.json
3. `snap.py` - snap pick times to word/segment boundaries
4. `moments.py` - moments.md CRUD plus channel-has / channel-mark dedupe log
5. `render_clip.py` - 1080x1080 face-centred crop per shot (letterbox over-shoulder / no-face), ASS karaoke captions (yellow spoken / white waiting), sidecar .srt, mark moments row cut

Keep the publisher's live copies under `/workspace/podcast-clips/` as the reference. If this imported bot is missing them, recreate from that reference or from a prior export of this skill that included the full script bodies.

skills.name: Podcast Clipper Getting Started
skills.description: First conversation with a new owner of the Podcast Clipper bot, or when the owner asks to set up or change which podcasts, niche, voice or clip settings it uses.
skills.content:
---
name: Podcast Clipper Getting Started
description: >-
  First conversation with a new owner of the Podcast Clipper bot, or when the
  owner asks to set up or change which podcasts, niche, voice or clip settings
  it uses.
---
# Getting started

Open with one line: "I turn podcast episodes into 8-12 square, captioned clips, each with ready-to-post X drafts in your voice."

Then ask ONE question at a time, waiting for each answer:
1. Which podcasts or YouTube channels should I watch? (names or URLs)
2. What's your niche, and which angles do you want clips to hit? (e.g. AI chips, investing, founders)
3. What's your X handle? Paste or link 3-5 of your own posts you like so I can learn your voice.
4. How many post versions per clip, 3, 4 or 5?
5. Want me to watch those channels and clip new episodes automatically when they drop?

After the answers:
- Save memories: watched sources (with channel URLs), niche/angles, X handle, versions per clip, auto-watch yes/no.
- Read the posts they gave (fetch them if linked) and save style notes as a memory: length, tone, hook style, emoji use, punctuation habits, words they avoid. Never invent personal facts about the owner.
- If auto-watch is yes: create a routine (e.g. hourly, or every 15 min on known release days) that checks each source for an episode newer than the last one recorded in memory; when one appears, tell the owner it dropped, run the Podcast Clipper skill on it, and record it as processed so it's never clipped twice.
- Confirm the setup back in 2-3 lines and offer to clip a recent episode now as a test.
